accounting.rationale: Original PDF117, printed103, lines3-7: object-attribute vocabulary, declared-type mechanisms and two attribute-specification routes. The six subdivisions retain the definitions and permissions without creating an S requirement, no-op effect or automatic rejection oracle.

Type and rank, with any type parameters and other use-determining properties, describe data objects. PENDING documentary plan: bind the 3.42 constant/variable/subobject definition to one named constant and one variable under C810; no value need be read to establish the category.
Attributes is the collective term for these properties. PENDING terminology reconciliation with 7.1, 7.2, 8.5 and 15.3; no classifier program or additional executable facet.

An explicit type declaration is one declared-type route. PENDING canonical source-use plan: retain the R703 intrinsic and TYPE-derived declarations and the 8.2/R801 statement owner; TYPE(*) and CLASS(*) retain their separately specified absence of declared type. A new wrapper would not prove a new rule.

The initial-letter route is governed by 8.7, including local mappings, host inheritance and IMPLICIT NONE, rather than an unconditional default-integer/default-real inference. PENDING finite source-use matrix: explicit mapping, inherited mapping, default mapping and no-mapping contexts, with original 8.7 ownership and no invented local mandatory diagnostic.

The 8.5 attributes can be specified in a type declaration where their defining contexts permit it. PENDING source-use matrix: the nineteen R802 alternatives, including both access keywords and all INTENT alternatives, remain owned by R802 and the relevant 8.5 definitions. The permission does not make incompatible combinations conforming.

Separate specification statements are an alternative mechanism, not permission to duplicate an attribute. PENDING source-use plan: preserve C815_valid and its ALLOCATABLE-before-type and DIMENSION-after-type contexts, compare the original 8.6 forms, and retain C815's cross-statement exclusion. Initialization ordering still comes from 8.4; no new source-use mechanism is assumed approved.

Original PDF117 lines8-9: function characteristics and the type/rank/type-parameter correspondence to its result. This is not identity of the procedure and result object and not a transfer of every other attribute.

A function has use-determining characteristics including type and rank and possibly parameters. PENDING documentary pairing with 15.3.1 and 15.6.2.2; do not create a meaningless success-only function program.

The result supplies the function type. PENDING finite canonical contexts: external function declaration, function prefix, and RESULT(r) with a result-object declaration. Keep the prefix/result single-typing rule and C1570; C809 does not forbid internal/module result-object declarations.

The result supplies the function rank. PENDING source-use comparison of scalar, explicit-shape array and deferred-shape allocatable/pointer results under 15.6.2.2 and C816; a function-name declaration is not a general object array declarator.

The result supplies type parameters. PENDING source-use comparison of constant CHARACTER LEN, eligible assumed/deferred result length, and a complete PDT result; preserve C702/C726 and 15.6.2.2 qualifications instead of making the 7.2 local explanation a universal ban.
Original PDF117 lines10-11: the subroutine category lacks type/rank/type parameters but admits other attributes. No S ID or no-op execution is allocated.
PENDING source-use comparison of a SUBROUTINE statement and a FUNCTION statement under 15.6.2; no fabricated local type inquiry on a subroutine and no local diagnostic policy.
PENDING documentary separation of a subroutine from its scalar/array dummy data objects. A dummy's rank is not the subroutine's rank.
PENDING documentary separation of procedure attributes from type parameters of dummy objects; no KIND, LEN or raw-representation oracle on a subroutine.

Other subroutine attributes remain possible in their canonical contexts. PENDING finite source-use pair: an external subroutine and a pure subroutine under 8.5.9/15.7, without importing function type declarations or claiming purity from an empty run.
